strategy.summary: Reproduce the mpmath issue 838/839 longdouble/precision expectation on x86-64 Linux with CPython 3.12 and numpy<2.1, where np.float128 is 80-bit extended (64-bit mantissa). Run the developer's test_compatibility with the test diff applied to the buggy revision f04fa498d947 and check the transition. Caveat: the reproducing diff changes only test expectations, so on x86-64 the transition shows the test's precision assumption, not the alpha steffensen defect. The steffensen doctest on alpha cannot be reproduced on this platform and is listed as a risk.

pinned_because: numpy<2.1: documented in pyproject.toml tests extras and applies because python_version<3.13; numerically relevant since it sets the np.float128 behaviour
pytest>=6: documented in pyproject.toml tests extras
python 3.12: taken from the issue traceback; 3.8 to 3.13 are all documented as supported
packaging: unbounded in the evidence (no documented constraint, no era entry); unpinned latest chosen because test_compatibility imports packaging.version
pexpect, ipython, hypothesis, matplotlib: omitted because the selected tests do not import them; matplotlib is excluded anyway on PyPy and python>=3.13

strategy.reproducing_test: mpmath/tests/test_convert.py::test_compatibility, with the developer's diff applied: under 'if hasattr(np, float128)', mp.prec = 64 replaces mp.prec = 113, and the expected value becomes mpf('0.841470984807896506653') in place of mpf('0.841470984807896506664590813295845351'). Optional steffensen doctest check: python -m pytest --doctest-modules mpmath/calculus/optimization.py -k steffensen -q
strategy.success_criterion: Buggy revision with the test diff applied: test_compatibility should FAIL at the float128 comparison, because the 64-bit longdouble value (about 0.8414709848078965066525) is compared at prec 113 against the 21-digit-precision decimal 0.841470984807896506664590813295845351, which differs at about 1e-20. Fixed revision with the same test: test_compatibility should PASS, because at prec 64 both sides round to the same 64-bit mantissa. Transition: FAIL on buggy, PASS on fixed. This holds only where np.float128 is 80-bit extended; elsewhere the test is not a valid transition check.
strategy.numerical_probe: Print np.finfo(np.longdouble).nmant and mp.npconvert(np.float128('0.841470984807896506652502321630298954')) at prec 64 and 113 to confirm the 64-bit mantissa before running pytest.

input_output_examples.expected_output: equal in the fixed test at prec 64 against mpf('0.841470984807896506653')

risks: Platform dependence: the defect was observed on alpha and fails on MIPS64 per the evidence. Those platforms use a different longdouble format (alpha and MIPS64 do not provide 80-bit extended), so the observed behaviour cannot be reproduced on x86-64 Linux. The steffensen 0-versus-(-1.2197e-239) difference is a platform/libm underflow effect, not something this environment will show.

The steffensen doctest fix (f-string replacing printf-style '%20g', closes #838) is a library/format change not present in the reproducing test diff; the test diff alone does not show it. Verify the buggy-vs-fixed transition for steffensen separately, and do not treat the test_compatibility transition as proof of the alpha defect.

On aarch64 Linux or other IEEE-quad longdouble platforms, the old prec 113 expectation passes, so the transition would not appear there. On Windows (longdouble equal to double) np.float128 is absent and the block is skipped, so the test is vacuous.
numpy>=2.1 or other versions may change np.float128 handling; the pin numpy<2.1 is documented (explicit) and should be kept, not replaced by an era-inferred choice.
The added test_issue_471 and test_issue_472 in test_gammazeta.py (bernpoly with inf) are unrelated to the alpha evidence and to test_compatibility; they are not part of this reproduction.
Doctest collection through pytest --doctest-modules may behave differently from the project's own doctest runner; if the steffensen doctest is run, confirm the mp.dps = 15 context matches.
Unbounded dependencies (packaging, pexpect, ipython, hypothesis): the choice here is unpinned latest packaging and omission of the others, which is a chosen strategy, not a documented constraint.

oracle.reference_source: developer test expectation in the PR diff (mpf string comparison)
oracle.why: mpf equality at a fixed precision is exact; the transition depends on the 64-bit longdouble mantissa rounding to the same value as the 21-digit decimal at prec 64.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On the buggy revision with the test diff applied, the assertion at prec 113 is not met: the 64-bit longdouble value is compared with the higher-precision decimal, and they differ near 1e-20, so the equality assertion fails.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the fixed revision with the test diff applied, at prec 64 the float128 value and mpf('0.841470984807896506653') round to the same 64-bit mantissa, so the equality holds and the test passes.
